objective: Complete TASK-007 by adding the outstanding mutation-sensitive and fallback-path regressions around the already-landed hook hardening, without redeclaring production files that will be unchanged from the implementation baseline.
requirements: Adopt the rescope route for the current working tree: treat the existing fail-closed Stop guard, non-blocking SessionStart read degradation, explicit UTF-8 stdout emission, binary-mode classification, AST cache, and resilience tests as already-landed behavior rather than implementation work produced by this baseline.

Modify only test_utf8_io.py and test_hook_resilience.py; do not declare or edit the already-hardened hook implementations because they are expected to be byte-identical to the implementation baseline.

Restore and strengthen Utf8RoundTripTests.test_context_block_round_trips_unicode and Utf8RoundTripTests.test_context_file_bytes_are_utf8 in place so their fixtures write genuine non-ASCII JSON bytes by forcing ensure_ascii=False only within the test harness, while leaving production json.dumps behavior unchanged.

Keep Utf8RoundTripTests.test_ascii_content_is_byte_for_byte_unchanged and strengthen it, if needed, to compare produced bytes with an independently constructed expected ASCII byte sequence rather than a decode-and-reencode identity.

Extend the existing AuditDiscriminatesTests class with named mutation regressions for the context write encoding, context read encoding, context byte encoding, and ASCII-compatibility encoding claims.

Each encoding mutation regression must execute its specific Utf8RoundTripTests method against both the unmodified in-memory orchestrator module and a uniquely mutated in-memory module with the relevant encoding keyword removed, asserting an unmodified-pass followed by a mutated-fail transition.
Make omitted encoding deterministic in mutation tests with a narrowly scoped and reliably restored Path.open shim using UTF-16 as the default; do not depend on the host locale.

Add SessionStartEmitsUtf8Tests.test_stdout_without_a_buffer_still_emits, exercising emit() with a stdout replacement that has no buffer and asserting non-cp1252 text is emitted without raising or being lost.
Strengthen AuditCacheTests with a named parse-count regression that clears _CALL_CACHE, wraps ast.parse with a counter, audits the same path twice, and asserts exactly one parse.
Add a named regression proving calls_in_source remains uncached by auditing two different source strings and observing distinct results.
Retain the existing binary-mode tests proving open(path, 'rb'), os.fdopen(fd, 'rb'), Path.open('rb'), and keyword binary modes are not offenders while text calls without encoding remain offenders.
Add Python39CompatibilityTests.test_touched_sources_parse_with_python39_grammar for both files modified by this contract using ast.parse(feature_version=(3, 9)).
Preserve the existing production encoding arguments and valid hook behavior; the new tests must not require changes to .ai/hooks/stop_guard.py or .ai/hooks/session_start.py.

files_to_modify.purpose: Restore the two misleading F4 test identities with real non-ASCII byte fixtures, add pass-to-fail behavioral mutation proofs, make the ASCII compatibility assertion independent, prove parse-cache behavior, and add Python 3.9 grammar coverage for the touched tests.
Add direct coverage for SessionStart emit() when stdout has no binary buffer while retaining the existing subprocess guards for fail-closed Stop behavior and UTF-8 SessionStart output.

acceptance_criteria.statement: As a deliberate regression guard over already-landed hook code, malformed UTF-8 in either Stop input exits 2 with a reason on stderr, and the existing completed and incomplete write-back contracts remain intact.

SessionStart continues to emit Japanese text as UTF-8 and exit 0 through the normal subprocess path, and the newly covered stdout-without-buffer fallback emits the same text without raising or losing it.

The restored F4 tests and strengthened F5 test are encoding-sensitive, and every named mutation test runs its specific Utf8RoundTripTests method against both the unmodified and uniquely mutated in-memory orchestrator modules and asserts a pass-then-fail transition when the relevant encoding argument is removed.

Binary positional and keyword modes remain correctly classified, repeated path audits invoke ast.parse exactly once, and calls_in_source remains uncached so different in-memory source mutations are independently parsed.
Both files changed by this contract parse with Python 3.9 grammar, and the complete repository unittest suite is non-empty and passes under the orchestrator-provided validation interpreter.
acceptance_criteria.verify: {python} -m unittest -v test_utf8_io.Python39CompatibilityTests.test_touched_sources_parse_with_python39_grammar && {python} -c "import unittest; s=unittest.defaultTestLoader.discover('.'); n=s.countTestCases(); print('discovered %d tests' % n); r=unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2).run(s); raise SystemExit(0 if n > 0 and r.wasSuccessful() else 1)"

acceptance_criteria.statement: Full runtime execution on Python 3.9 and 3.12 is explicitly delegated to the unchanged CI matrix and must be confirmed by CI outside local acceptance validation; this command verifies only that both required versions remain configured in that matrix.
acceptance_criteria.verify: {python} -c "from pathlib import Path; s=Path('.github/workflows/ci.yml').read_text(encoding='utf-8'); assert 'python-version: [\"3.9\", \"3.12\"]' in s and 'run: python -m unittest -v' in s"

constraints: Use only the Python standard library.

The implementation baseline will be captured from the current tree; .ai/hooks/stop_guard.py, .ai/hooks/session_start.py, and other already-modified working-tree files are not part of this contract and must remain byte-identical during TASK-007 implementation.
A Stop guard failure to read verdict-dependent input must continue to fail closed with exit code 2 and a reason; SessionStart must continue to degrade visibly without blocking.
Do not weaken or delete an existing test; restore the two F4 identities and strengthen F4 and F5 in place.
Do not change production json.dumps behavior; ensure_ascii=False is confined to test fixtures that expose encoding behavior.
Keep the explicit UTF-8 production file I/O introduced by TASK-006 exactly as currently established.

Do not change newline translation, _support.py text I/O, diff-scope base selection, unrelated attribute-call classification, hook behavior, or any behavior beyond the six findings and their missing regression proof.
Acceptance commands may use only the orchestrator-provided {python} interpreter; multi-version runtime coverage belongs to CI because a local criterion cannot portably reach a second interpreter.
The complete suite check must reject zero discovered tests and output without a successful test result.
Do not modify .github/workflows/ci.yml, task evidence, state.json, review artifacts, schemas, or other orchestrator-owned state.

Approval must be bound by the orchestrator to the canonical revised plan file and the SHA-256 of its exact bytes before implementation; canonical plan selection is an approval precondition, not an implementation change authorized by this contract.
Workflow behavior checks in AC-1 and the already-landed portions of AC-2 are deliberate regression guards, not claims that this implementation produced the hook changes.
Maintain runtime compatibility with Python 3.9 and Python 3.12, with actual execution on both versions required from the existing CI matrix.
risks: The hook hardening and most F1, F2, F3, F5, and F6 changes are already present before the immutable implementation baseline exists; redeclaring those production files would create an automatic declared-but-unchanged failure. This plan therefore respecifies the remaining test work instead of pretending to reproduce already-landed bytes.

The earlier production architecture was structurally sound; the rejected plans failed because their declared file state, provenance, selectors, and verification contract did not match the working tree. A replan cannot repair an implementation bug that is already fixed, so the remaining work is regression proof and test precision.
AC-1 is intentionally non-material because it checks already-landed hook behavior; its passing result must not be interpreted as proof that the current implementation phase changed the hook.

The stdout-without-buffer fallback writes through a text stream supplied by an embedding environment; a realistic no-buffer test must verify content and exceptions without claiming it can override an arbitrary stream's own lossy codec.

Mutation tests can give false confidence if they merely AST-audit mutated text or remove an unrelated keyword; each test must uniquely target the production call and run the covered behavioral method against normal and mutated modules.
Monkeypatching Path.open, json.dumps, sys.stdout, or ast.parse can contaminate unrelated tests unless every patch is scoped and restored with cleanup even when the assertion fails.
A UTF-16 omitted-encoding default is intentionally hostile and deterministic, but the shim must preserve explicitly encoded calls and binary modes so failures identify only the removed encoding.
Caching solely by path can become stale for changed files; the production audit remains path-cached for stable repository files while mutation tests must use the uncached source-level path.

Python 3.9 feature-version parsing checks syntax only, not runtime API compatibility; AC-6 transparently delegates actual 3.9 and 3.12 execution to CI rather than implying the local interpreter proves both.

The current canonical task state reportedly names an older plan despite a newer plan version; approval is unsafe until the orchestrator points to and hashes this revised plan. That state transition is outside worker implementation scope.
Unrelated pre-existing working-tree changes and the acknowledged diff-base problem can affect orchestration, but this contract authorizes changes only to the two declared test files.
test_strategy: Run the existing Stop guard subprocess tests as a non-material regression guard, covering malformed implementation.md and context.jsonl bytes, explanatory stderr, exit code 2, and unchanged allow/block behavior.

Run the existing SessionStart subprocess tests for Japanese UTF-8 output and unreadable-input degradation, then directly load session_start.py and invoke emit() with a capture stream lacking .buffer to exercise and assert the fallback branch.

For each restored F4 test, force ensure_ascii=False only in the fixture so context.jsonl contains genuine high bytes, assert the unmodified module succeeds, and assert a module with the uniquely relevant encoding removed fails under the deterministic UTF-16 default.

Construct the expected ASCII JSONL bytes independently for the F5 test, accounting only for the established serialization and platform newline behavior, then use the same normal-pass/mutated-fail harness to prove its encoding sensitivity.
Keep mutation modules and monkeypatches in memory or temporary directories; restore Path.open, json.dumps, sys.stdout, ast.parse, imported modules, and working-directory state with cleanup guards.

Clear _CALL_CACHE, count ast.parse invocations across two text_io_calls calls for one path, and assert one parse; separately feed calls_in_source two distinct strings and assert distinct audit results.
Run the focused BinaryModeClassificationTests to cover built-in open, os.fdopen, Path.open, keyword binary modes, text counterexamples, and os.open exclusion.

Parse test_utf8_io.py and test_hook_resilience.py with Python 3.9 grammar, run a guarded non-empty full suite under {python}, and require the unchanged CI matrix to execute the full suite on Python 3.9 and 3.12 before completion.
